I Know – About Emergency Fund
An emergency fund or a rainy day fund, as the name suggests, is that cash reserve— your savings kept aside 
for any unprecedented event happening or an emergency. It is a good way to reduce your risk to income; loss 
in income or a sudden dip. 
How much to save for a ‘rainy day’?
It is generally recommended to maintain an emergency fund that can cover your living expenses for at least 
three months. But if your job is less secure or you run a business or are self-employed, then you probably 
should save to cover your expenses for six months or more.
Where to save?
Money in the emergency fund should be kept in a savings account—separate from your other savings 
accounts—that is easily accessible. You should ideally fund your emergency account before any of your other 
savings accounts.
